title: Sync from live reads the copy's database into its scratch schema even while the copy is still settling after a chat turn (a table dropped, purged, created or truncated during the read is a change to read again, not a stop); a real stop names the server's error with no value of the site
steps: S1: node --test packages/fleet/tracy-fleet-operation/test/live-sync-copy-load.test.mjs (real MariaDB in a container of its own)
expect: S1: a site table or a _tracy_trash_ table dropped between the list and the dump: load_ours returns 0 and the scratch schema holds every table of the site
S1: a table created after the list is in the scratch schema (never left out silently)
S1: a TRUNCATE during the dump (Error 1412) is read again: load_ours returns 0
S1: a copy busy for ~3 s (snapshots, a listed table dropped and made again, rows written) loads once it settles: return 0
S1: a broken view still stops (return 2) and LOAD_OURS_WHY carries 1356 with no table or view name
S1: db_error_line keeps the error code, cuts at the first quote, skips the docker client's warnings
S2: merge's MERGE_FAILED for the copy's load carries LOAD_OURS_WHY
fence: A copy that is merely busy never stops a sync; a stop always says why without a value of the site

tests: the copy at rest loads whole
a table that goes between the list and its dump
a table that comes after the list
a table emptied by TRUNCATE while the dump reads
a copy the server cannot read still stops
a copy busy for a few seconds after a chat turn
the reason is the first error line
both scripts check their scratch loads by hand
